children: rose over 6% in October, ahead of the broader S&P 500 index, which remained largely flat during the period. The sector benefitted from firms in the apparel, retail, restaurants, fitness, entertainment, and consumer services industries, which were among its strongest performers during the period.

“Consumer stocks performed well during a volatile October that witnessed significant sector rotation by investors. As earnings season got underway, it was clear that consumers proved resilient yet again to inflation pressures, and a solid labor market continues to support spending. With oil prices high, risks clearly still remain, but it has proven premature to bet against the American consumer,” Seeking Alpha analyst Seeking Profits said.
Top consumer discretionary gainers of the month

climbed over 11% following its third-quarter results in October, reaching a new 52-week high. The games and toy company reported a better-than-expected Q3 print and raised its full-year financial outlook. Hasbro reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.90 on revenue of $1.6B. The standout performer was the Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment, where revenue climbed 31%. Earlier in the month, the firm also announced the official opening of its new Wizards of the Coast Studios location.

“Hasbro reported excellent quarterly results, and its MAGIC: The Gathering franchise has become a differentiator thanks to its loyal fanbase of collectors. Additionally, tariff pressures from last year have largely faded, and upcoming film releases should support toy sales. I have been bullish on HAS and reiterated my buy post-earnings given excellent cash generation and sustained growth in MAGIC,” as per Seeking Profits.

became the second-highest gainer this month, driven by this post-earnings shares rally. On Thursday, the cruise operator beat top-and-bottom-line expectations, raised its outlook for the year, and appointed a new CFO.

“The cruising sector can be highly impacted by the oil crisis, given the significant fuel costs within operations, but travel spending has proven quite durable. Norwegian’s appeal to higher-income consumers also leaves it less exposed to affordability pressures and better able to pass on price increases. With solid financial markets creating favorable wealth effect dynamics, I believe spending can remain solid within its core demographic,” the analyst added.
Top consumer discretionary detractors of the month

lost significant ground this month as it continues to be mired in controversies accusing the travel company of fraudulent practices. The European Commission has opened formal proceedings against its subsidiary Booking.com under the Digital Services Act to investigate whether the platform does enough to remove fraudulent listings and stop phishing scams. The platform could also face a Federal Trade Commission
investigation over allegations that subsidiary Priceline.com uses third-party hotel booking services that charge hidden fees in violation of consumer protection laws.

“Booking.com faces ongoing regulatory scrutiny, and European enforcement against American firms continues to be a risk in any tech and tech-adjacent sectors. Additionally, there is concern that AI agents could disrupt “middlemen” businesses like BKNG’s and undermine ad-related revenue. Meta’s Muse Agent has re-intensified those fears, and I expect AI overhangs to persist for some time as companies like Booking will need to prove out the resilience of their model in an agentic environment,” Seeking Profits noted.

Consumer sector earnings are likely to remain in focus over the coming weeks, particularly following Amazon’s performance. The holiday shopping season, which kicks off in November, is also expected to offer valuable insights into consumer spending behavior amid a volatile macroeconomic environment. Oil prices will remain another key area of interest, given their potential impact on consumer spending patterns.

title: Hasbro leads consumer discretionary sector in October as Booking Holdings slumps amid antitrust heat
